zulm

zulm builds computation graphs of tensors in R, runs them on the CPU, differentiates them and trains their parameters, through upstream ggml, the C tensor library behind llama.cpp and whisper.cpp.

Upstream ggml, unmodified and current, as a small, safe, reproducible R substrate for training and running models on the CPU.

Two use cases size the package:

  • Training. Small and medium neural networks trained in R on the CPU with ggml’s autograd and its AdamW and SGD optimisers, with results that reproduce bit for bit at a fixed seed. The first consumer is zuflow, which trains and samples an event-sequence generator.
  • Inference. Pretrained transformer checkpoints of up to a few hundred million parameters, loaded from GGUF or safetensors and run without Python, LibTorch or a GPU toolchain. The first consumer is zukzeit, which runs time-series foundation models.

zulm is under development toward its first CRAN release. Nothing of the R interface is built yet; the roadmap tracks progress.

Installation

You can install the development version of zulm from GitHub with:

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("pedrobtz/zulm")
